topics.label: Introduction and lecture overview
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer opens the session by linking histopathology practicals to cellular transformation and outlining the lecture's learning outcomes.

topics.label: Tumor viruses, cellular oncogene discovery, and transformation assays
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics trace how the study of transforming tumor viruses led to the discovery of cellular proto-oncogenes and experimental assays for cell transformation.

topics.label: Functional classifications and mutational mechanisms of oncogenes and tumor suppressors
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the concepts of oncogenes versus tumor suppressor genes and demonstrate how dominant, recessive, and dominant-negative mutations disrupt regulatory pathways such as the cell cycle.

topics.label: Mechanisms, cellular consequences, and stepwise progression of genetic instability
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the molecular defects that generate sequence and chromosomal instability and how this instability accelerates multi-step tumor progression.

topics.label: Hereditary cancer predisposition and tumor evolution
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how inherited germline mutations in caretaker and gatekeeper genes accelerate cancer development and shape tumor evolution.

topics.label: Conclusion and reading recommendations
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the session, offers to answer questions, recommends supplementary reading, and previews the upcoming lecture.
